title: Algebra foundations: linear equations
description: A short original starter course with worked examples and a practice test. Use the linked textbook to cross-check concepts; this is not a full examination syllabus.
syllabus: Equality; one- and two-step linear equations; distribution; variables on both sides; special cases; fixed fractional coefficients; simple word problems. Original explanations and questions, with OpenStax Elementary Algebra 2e Chapter 2 as a reference. Teacher review is required.

lessons.title: Equality and one-step equations
lessons.content:
An equation states that two expressions have the same value. A solution is a value that makes that statement true. To keep the solution set unchanged, add or subtract the same number on both sides. Multiplication or division by the same nonzero number also preserves equality.

For x + a = b, subtract a from each side. For ax = b with a not equal to zero, divide both sides by a. Check a proposed solution by substituting it into the original equation. A transformed equation can look simpler while a copied sign error changes its solution.
lessons.workedExample:
Solve 5x - 6 = 14.
Add 6 to each side: 5x = 20.
Divide each side by 5: x = 4.
Check: 5(4) - 6 = 14, so the solution is correct.
lessons.revisionNotes: Keep equality balanced. Never divide by zero. Substitute into the original equation to check.
lessons.subject: Mathematics

lessons.title: Brackets and variables on both sides
lessons.content:
Use the distributive property before collecting terms: a(b + c) = ab + ac. A minus sign outside brackets changes the sign of every enclosed term. Combine like terms, then move variable terms together using equal operations on both sides.

If all variable terms cancel, inspect what remains. A false statement such as 0 = 5 means there is no solution. A true statement such as 0 = 0 means every allowed value satisfies the equation.
lessons.workedExample:
Solve 3(x + 2) = 2x + 11.
Distribute: 3x + 6 = 2x + 11.
Subtract 2x: x + 6 = 11.
Subtract 6: x = 5.
Check: 3(5 + 2) = 21 and 2(5) + 11 = 21.
lessons.revisionNotes: Distribute to every term. Keep track of negative signs. Cancellation can produce one solution, no solution or infinitely many solutions.

lessons.title: Fractional coefficients and translating a statement
lessons.content:
When denominators are fixed nonzero numbers, multiply the entire equation by a common multiple of those denominators. This removes fractional coefficients. Apply the multiplier to every term on both sides.

When modelling a word problem, define the unknown and its unit first. Translate the stated relationship into an equation, solve it and check whether the result makes sense in context. This lesson covers numerical denominators; expressions with a variable in a denominator also require domain restrictions.
lessons.workedExample:
Solve x/3 + 2 = 7.
Subtract 2: x/3 = 5.
Multiply by 3: x = 15.
Check: 15/3 + 2 = 7.

A notebook costs n rupees. Three notebooks and a 12-rupee pen cost 87 rupees.
3n + 12 = 87, so 3n = 75 and n = 25 rupees.
lessons.revisionNotes: Multiply every term when clearing denominators. Define units. Check the solution against both the original equation and the story.

Add 5 to obtain 2x = 18, then divide by 2.

questions.prompt: What is the solution set of x + 2 = x + 7?
questions.explanation: Subtract x: 2 = 7 is false, so there is no solution.

questions.prompt: What is the solution set of 2(x + 1) = 2x + 2?
questions.explanation: Expanding the left side gives the right side for every real x.

questions.prompt: Two identical pens and a 10-rupee notebook cost 50 rupees. What is the price of one pen?
questions.explanation: If a pen costs p rupees, 2p + 10 = 50. Thus 2p = 40 and p = 20.
